claims.text: The hotel is in Lisbon's historic center, between Chiado and Bairro Alto.

findings.quote: Bairro Alto Hotel is located in the historic center of Lisbon in a prestigious and emblematic area
it is located between the elegant and cosmopolitan Chiado and the bohemian Bairro Alto

claims.text: Praca Luis de Camoes is visible from the hotel's entrance.

findings.quote: From the entrance of the hotel we see Praça Luís de Camões

claims.text: The hotel first opened in 2005.

findings.quote: First opened in 2005

claims.text: The hotel reopened in 2019 after a three-year renovation.

findings.quote: It reopened in 2019 following a three-year renovation.

claims.text: Rooms have soundproofed windows that block out the noise of passing trams.

findings.quote: Special mention goes to the soundproofed windows, which block out the rumble of the city’s yellow trams as they pass.

claims.text: The ground-floor Patisserie makes Portuguese sweet and savoury pastries in the hotel throughout the day.

findings.quote: The Patisserie on the ground ﬂoor, with an unobstructed view to the Luís de Camões square, oﬀers a daily selection of typically Portuguese sweet and savoury pastries freshly made in the hotel throughout the day.

claims.text: The Mezzanine bar on the ground floor serves healthy meals throughout the day.

findings.quote: Welcoming and cosy, on a mezzanine on the ground ﬂoor, this bar is the hotel’s meeting point par excellence. You can enjoy our menu of healthy meals throughout the day.

claims.text: The hotel's terrace has a view over the city and the Tejo river.

findings.quote: This is the place for those who want to enjoy an incomparable view over the city and the Tejo river.

claims.text: The wellness center has a Susanne Kaufmann spa and a gym.

findings.quote: Even with its on-trend Susanne Kaufmann spa, the wellness center, which also includes a gym

claims.text: The hotel is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.

findings.quote: A member of The Leading Hotels of the World, Bairro Alto Hotel is a pioneer

claims.text: The hotel offers guests a guide to Lisbon with off-radar suggestions.

findings.quote: There’s also a useful guide to Lisbon with some genuinely off-radar suggestions.

claims.text: Tram 28 passes through Chiado near the hotel.

findings.quote: The harmonious light of Lisbon shines on the streets as we cross to Chiado. Under the watchful eye of Fernando Pessoa, a tram goes by: the "28", as it is known

claims.text: The hotel is housed in an 18th-century building with a primrose yellow exterior on Praca Luis de Camoes.

findings.quote: The distinctive, primrose yellow exterior of the 18th-century building that houses the Bairro Alto Hotel has an impressive perch on the edge of Chiado’s landmark square, the Praça Luís de Camões

claims.text: A sixth-floor bar is reserved for hotel residents, with views over the rooftops to the River Tagus.

findings.quote: only hotel residents can use the sixth-floor bar, a secret spot where blue skies stretch out over the rooftops to the River Tagus

claims.text: The fifth-floor restaurant serves Portuguese cuisine created by Chef Bruno Rocha.

findings.quote: Go up to the 5th floor and be amazed by the best of Portuguese cuisine, created by Chef Bruno Rocha

claims.text: The hotel spans four Pombal-era buildings, so no two rooms are the same.

findings.quote: The hotel is larger and now spans four Pombal-era buildings, so no two rooms are the same.

claims.text: The interiors include specially commissioned pieces by Portuguese artists such as Vasco Araujo and Rui Chafes.
